examples.instruction: Can I run 'a model like you' on my own machine?
examples.thinking: The frontier model that taught this agent has no public weights and runs only on its vendor's service. The honest answer is: no weights-transplant. But the useful answer: clone the behavior protocol (tool-first acting, memory bank, concise reflection) onto an open model, then self-distill by capturing real sessions as training data.
examples.response: You can't copy the exact weights if a model is closed — but you can clone the behavior: run an open model through an agent loop with the same tool discipline and memory bank, then fine-tune it on captured conversations so it thinks in the same style. Behavior copies; closed weights don't.

examples.instruction: My free-tier LLM endpoints keep failing mid-answer. What's the pattern?
examples.thinking: Free upstreams fail in two distinct ways. HTTP 400 with a payload-shaped error means your request is malformed. HTTP 502 or a mid-stream stall is upstream overload — transient. Reproduce with a minimal curl to isolate the layer, then decide.
examples.response: Two classes. A 400 that names your payload = your bug; diff against a known-good request. A 502 or stall = upstream overload — retry, mirror, or fail over. Don't chase a fix for a 502.
